title: eGovPH superapp to include SSS services, digital ID

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – The Social Security System (SSS) and the Department of Information and Communications Technology (DICT) signed a data-sharing agreement to bring the MySSS card and select member services to the eGovPH superapp.
Members will also be able to view their contribution history, their total number of contributions, and employer information on integration.

“Our members should not have to visit multiple offices or use multiple applications just to access basic services. Through eGovPH superapp, we are making it easier for Filipinos to check their contributions, verify their membership status, and access their MySSS Card—all in one place,” Chief Executive Officer Victor Alfonso A. Limlingan said.
RELATED STORY: Siargao now has upgraded 5G Internet coverage

Members can already access their information and contributions through the MySSS app. This will still be active when the integration is complete as government bodies see this as an additional convenience.
DICT and SSS also expressed intent on expanding the superapp for social-protection access for freelancers and online professionals.
Limlingan and DICT Secretary Robert Joseph M. de Claro and SSS President signed the agreement on Oct. 21

“This partnership marks a major step in making SSS services more accessible and convenient for our members. By integrating the digital MySSS Card and key services into the eGovPH superapp, we are bringing social security closer to every Filipino—right at their fingertips,” Limlingan said.
